title: Bordered table with alignment
prompt:
Print the data below as a text table with the five columns `item`, `qty`, `price`, `amount` and `note`. The data rows, in order, given as item, quantity, unit price in cents, and note:
- bolts, 12000, 5, `bulk`
- hex nuts, 350, 12, `galvanized`
- washers, 7, 123456, `special order`
- anchor, 1, 99, and an empty note
- rivets, 1500, 3, `aluminium`
- brackets, 24, 1050, `left-hand only`
Cell contents:
- `item` is the item name, left-aligned.
- `qty` is the quantity with a comma between every group of three digits counted from the right (`12,000`, `350`), right-aligned.
- `price` is the unit price and `amount` the quantity times the unit price, both written in dollars with the whole dollars grouped by commas like `qty` and exactly two digits after a point (123456 cents is `1,234.56`, 5 cents is `0.05`), right-aligned.
- `note` is the note, centered; a note longer than 10 characters is cut to its first 9 characters followed by `~`.
- After the data rows comes a total row: `TOTAL` in the item column, the sum of the quantities in the qty column, the sum of the amounts in the amount column, and empty price and note cells.
Each column is as wide as its longest cell, the header included. Header cells are aligned like the rest of their column. A left-aligned cell is padded with spaces on the right, a right-aligned cell on the left, and a centered cell gets half of the padding spaces on the left and the rest on the right (when the number of padding spaces is odd, the right side gets one more).
Layout, line by line: a border line; the header line; a border line made with `=` instead of `-`; one line per data row; a border line; the total row; a border line. A border line is `+`, then for each column the character `-` repeated (column width + 2) times followed by `+`. A row line is `| `, then the cells separated by ` | `, then ` |`.
